newsitem.title: UK: UK's popular Blair says he facing tough challenges.
newsitem.headline: UK's popular Blair says he facing tough challenges.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair, his popularity soaring after 100 hectic days in power, on Saturday promised to produce an annual progress report on the government's handling of "Great Britain Plc."
"I will make sure we never think we have a right to rule," said the modernist who transformed his socialist party and swept to a landslide election victory on May 1.
"It has been a busy 100 days," he said, boasting of independence for the Bank of England, lower class sizes in schools, more hospital spending and a crackdown on juvenile crime.
Blair, writing in the tabloid Sun, agreed that the honeymoon with British voters could not last forever and said: "I am aware some tough challenges lie ahead."
The new prime minister, who rescued the Labour Party from 18 years in the political wilderness, enjoys unparalleled support in opinion polls.
The latest in Friday's Daily Telegraph gave him an 83 percent approval rating -- the highest since polling began.
But some of the gloss has gone off the sparkling success story in the past two weeks with the opposition Conservatives fighting back to win a by-election.
A minister attacked for conflict of interest backed down and sold two million pounds worth of his shares.
A Scottish Labour member of parliament committed suicide, claiming he was the target of a smear campaign.
Foreign secretary Robin Cook left his wife of 28 years for his parliamentary aide.
Interest rates have risen four times, hitting homeowners hard with higher house loans.

But Blair defended his decisions, saying: "We were right to give independence to the Bank of England -- even though we knew that due to the last government's cowardice, interest rate rises were almost certain."
Blair said throughout the election campaign that Labour could never achieve a landslide triumph and that victory should never be taken for granted.
Now, with his popularity at an all-time high, he still wants to keep his government up to the mark.
"I have decided to issue an annual report on the government -- the equivalent of a chief executive's report on Great Britain Plc."

With another election highly unlikely before the turn of the century and Labour setting its sights on a decade in power, he said; "I want to make sure that we never lose sight of our main priorities."
The Independent newspaper asked all cabinet ministers to give an appraisal of their first three months at the helm and then concluded: "Mr Blair's first 100 days: We like what we see."
